core_obligations: Part (1): write the target as a filtered colimit of affine schemes, note that the fibre products with the source are affine because the map is representable and affine, and conclude that the source is an affine formal algebraic space (proof lines 4338-4345).
Part (2): observe that the index set in that presentation may be taken countable, so that the source is countably indexed as well (proof lines 4347-4351).

Parts (3) to (5): use the implications between types to see that the target is countably indexed, write both spaces as formal spectra of weakly admissible algebras, convert the map into a continuous algebra homomorphism and observe that it is taut, then apply the three ascent statements to obtain classicity, weak adicness and the adic* property for the source (proof lines 4353-4368).

Part (6): obtain the adic* property for the source from part (3), apply the criterion for Noetherian affine formal algebraic spaces to see that the stages of a presentation of the target are Noetherian, and then that the fibre products are Noetherian because the map is locally of finite type, and apply the criterion once more to conclude for the source (proof lines 4370-4385).
proof_roadmap: Part (1): the colimit presentation of the source (proof lines 4338-4345).
Parts (3) to (5): formal spectra, tautness and three ascent statements (proof lines 4353-4368).
Part (6): the Noetherian criterion used twice (proof lines 4370-4385).
difficulty_reason: For a representable affine map of fppf sheaves from X to an affine formal algebraic space Y, the lemma asserts that X is an affine formal algebraic space and that it inherits countable indexedness, countable indexedness together with classicity, weak adicness, the adic* property, and -- when Y is Noetherian and the map is locally of finite type -- Noetherianness (statement lines 4315-4336). The proof of the first part is a colimit argument: writing the target as a filtered colimit of affine schemes, the fibre products with X are affine because the map is representable and affine, and they present X as a colimit, which is exactly the shape required of an affine formal algebraic space (proof lines 4338-4345). The second part reads off countable indexedness because the index set may then be taken countable (proof lines 4347-4351). Parts (3), (4) and (5) are grouped: in each case the assumptions already imply that the target is countably indexed and weakly admissible, so the source is, and after writing both as formal spectra the map corresponds to a continuous algebra homomorphism, which the representability and affineness of the map make taut; the three properties are then transported by the three corresponding ascent statements for taut maps (proof lines 4353-4368). The last part combines the third with an implication between types to get the adic* property for the source, then applies the criterion for Noetherian affine formal algebraic spaces twice, once to learn that the stages of a presentation are Noetherian and once, after the fibre products are seen to be Noetherian because the map is locally of finite type, to conclude for the source (proof lines 4370-4385). The claim is H2: the parts are parallel consequences of one colimit description and of the tautness of the induced ring map, but each transfer is named and the Noetherian case requires a two-step use of a criterion.
